message.content:
Here’s a quick reference to the Canadian public‑holiday dates that create long weekends in 2023.  
(Only federal holidays that are observed nationwide are listed; provincial holidays that fall on a weekday will also give a long weekend in those provinces, but they’re not shown here.)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Observed (if different) | Long‑weekend span |
|-------------|---------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| **Jan 1** (Sun) | New Year’s Day | Observed **Jan 2** (Mon) | Jan 1–3 |
| **Apr 7** (Fri) | Good Friday | – | Apr 7–9 |
| **May 22** (Mon) | Victoria Day | – | May 20–22 |
| **Jul 1** (Sat) | Canada Day | Observed **Jul 3** (Mon) | Jul 1–3 |
| **Sep 4** (Mon) | Labour Day | – | Sep 2–4 |
| **Oct 9** (Mon) | Thanksgiving | – | Oct 7–9 |
| **Nov 11** (Mon) | Remembrance Day | – | Nov 9–11 |
| **Dec 25** (Mon) | Christmas | – | Dec 23–25 |

**Quick notes**

* **New Year’s Day** falls on a Sunday, so the official observance is Monday, Jan 2.  
* **Canada Day** falls on a Saturday, so the observance is Monday, Jul 3.  
* All other holidays listed above fall on a Monday or Friday, automatically creating a three‑day weekend.  

If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., Family Day in Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, etc.), let me know and I can add those as well.
